b+1 or simply b. A bipolar transistor only provides a limited amount of isolation between input
and output, which is about b. The higher the beta the better the isolation. A MOST, which has
a beta of infinity also provides infinite isolation.
The same is true for the input resistance. It can never be infinite, as for a MOST source
follower. It will be the resistance seen at the emitter, multiplied by the beta. This may be
insufficient for some preamplifiers (microphone, etc). This is why, quite often, a few emitter
followers are cascaded.

connection_description_excerpts.text: A Source follower is an ideal buffer in the sense that it translates an input voltage unattenuated (if the Bulk is connected to the Source) from an infinite impedance at the input to a mere 1/g m to the output.
This is not true for its bipolar equivalent, an emitter follower.
A bipolar transistor has Base current.
It can never be infinite, as for a MOST source follower.
It will be the resistance seen at the emitter, multiplied by the beta.
This is why, quite often, a few emitter followers are cascaded.
